mainTopic: Torah as protection from sin, and the Roman trials of רבי אלעזר בן פרטא (saved by miracles) and רבי חנינא בן תרדיון (sentenced to burning)
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a story about two חכמים who walk past the doorway of the זונות to fight their יצר, and the women pull back out of respect. One חכם explains with a פסוק in משלי that Torah guards a person from lewdness, and רבא explains that מזמה means 'from זמה.' The גמרא then returns to the Roman arrests of חכמים. רבי אלעזר בן פרטא, facing five charges, envies רבי חנינא בן תרדיון, who faces one. רבי חנינא answers that רבי אלעזר will be saved because he did Torah and גמילות חסדים, while רבי חנינא did only Torah, just as רב הונא teaches. The גמרא asks whether רבי חנינא really lacked charity and concludes that he gave, but not as much as he should have. At his trial, רבי אלעזר בן פרטא escapes every charge through clever answers and miracles, including help from אליהו against a witness. רבי חנינא בן תרדיון openly says he learns Torah because ה׳ commanded it, and he is sentenced to burning, his wife to death, and his daughter to a brothel. The גמרא begins explaining the reason for his burning, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Let's walk past the brothel and beat our inclination
steps.stepSummary: The first חכם finishes his reason: the יצר for עבודה זרה is gone. The second suggests walking past the זונות instead, so they can overcome their יצר and earn reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We can walk past the idol worship path] since that urge has been slaughtered. The other one said to him: Let's walk past the doorway of the prostitutes' house, overpower our urge, and get reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The first חכם finishes his words, and his friend suggests a harder test: walking past the house of זונות on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no reward for passing the עבודה זרה path, because that temptation no longer exists. The second חכם wants a real challenge. You only earn reward by fighting an urge that is actually there.

keyTerms.meaning: Its urge was 'slaughtered,' meaning that temptation no longer exists

steps.confusionAlert: They did not plan to go inside. The plan was only to walk past the doorway and win the fight against temptation.

phrases.english: since its urge has been slaughtered.
phrases.notes: This finishes the first חכם's words from before: they can pass the idol worship path, because that urge is gone.

phrases.english: The other one said to him:
Let us go by the entrance of the prostitutes' house
and overpower our inclination, and receive reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reward comes from overcoming a temptation that is still alive.

steps.title: The women pulled back before the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: When the two חכמים arrived, the זונות saw them and withdrew out of respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they arrived there, the prostitutes saw them and pulled back before them.
steps.whatsHappening: The story tells us what happened at the doorway. There was no test at all, because the women backed away when they saw the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים expected to struggle against temptation. Instead, the temptation went away on its own. This sets up the question in the next step: how did one of them know this would happen?

keyTerms.meaning: They humbled themselves and pulled back

phrases.english: When they arrived there,
they saw them, [the prostitutes],
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: they yielded and withdrew before them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the outcome of the plan from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זונות withdrew in front of the חכמים.

steps.title: How did you know this would happen?
steps.stepSummary: One חכם asks the other where he got the idea that this would happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From where do you know this?
steps.whatsHappening: One חכם asks the other for a source. He wants to know how his friend was so sure they would be protected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the friend had a reason to be confident they would not fall. The answer will be a פסוק showing that Torah protects a person.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?

phrases.english: He said to him: From where do you have this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the outcome in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that חכמים would be protected from this temptation.

steps.title: The פסוק: Torah guards you from lewdness
steps.stepSummary: He answers with the פסוק in משלי: 'מזמה תשמר עליך, תבונה תנצרכה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'From lewdness it will watch over you; understanding will guard you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The friend answers with a פסוק. It promises that wisdom, meaning Torah, protects a person from lewdness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads מזמה as 'from זמה,' meaning from lewdness. He reads תבונה as Torah. So someone who learns Torah is protected from this kind of sin.

phrases.english: He said to him:
"From lewdness it shall watch over you;
understanding shall guard you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in משלי promises that Torah guards a person from lewdness.
steps.whatToRemember: Torah learning protects a person from the יצר הרע of עריות.

steps.title: What does the word מזמה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבא what מזמה means. They suggest it might mean Torah, since זמה is translated as 'counsel,' and Torah is called 'counsel.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to רבא: What is 'מזמה'? If you say it means Torah: the Torah has the word 'זמה,' which we translate 'the counsel of sinners,' and it is written 'He made counsel wonderful, He made wisdom great.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the word in the פסוק. It offers a possible reading, that מזמה means Torah, and builds the argument for it. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the reasoning chain. The תרגום translates זמה as 'עצה' (counsel). In ישעיהו‎, ה׳'s Torah is called 'עצה.' So maybe זמה, and therefore מזמה, means Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggested reading that will be tested)
Lewdness; also explained as a plan or scheme
We translate it in the Aramaic תרגום

phrases.english: The Sages said to Rava:
What is "mezimma"?
If we say it means the Torah,
as "zimma" is written in it,
and we translate it: the counsel of sinners,
and it is written: "He made counsel wonderful, He made wisdom great."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the key word in the פסוק quoted in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מזמה in the פסוק.

steps.title: Then the פסוק should have said זמה
steps.stepSummary: If זמה means Torah, the פסוק should say 'זמה,' not 'מזמה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said 'זמה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 5. The extra letter מ doesn't fit if the word simply means Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof showed that זמה can mean counsel, or Torah. But the פסוק actually says מזמה, with a מ in front. So the 'Torah' reading leaves the extra letter unexplained.

phrases.english: If so, it should have said "zimma"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggested reading in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that מזמה means Torah.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word has an extra letter מ that the Torah reading does not explain.

steps.title: Read it as: from matters of זמה, the Torah guards you
steps.stepSummary: The מ means 'from.' The פסוק says that from lewd matters, the Torah (תבונה) will guard you.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: From a matter of lewdness it will watch over you; the Torah will guard you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the word differently. מזמה means 'from lewdness,' and the Torah is the תבונה, the 'understanding,' in the second half of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the extra מ makes sense: it means 'from.' The word for Torah is not מזמה but תבונה. This fits the story: Torah protected the חכמים from the זונות.
steps.whatToRemember: מזמה = 'from זמה (lewdness).' תבונה = Torah, which guards a person from that sin.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
from a matter of lewdness it shall watch over you,
the Torah shall guard you.
phrases.notes: So the word 'understanding' in the פסוק is the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzMaskana: מזמה means 'from lewdness,' and תבונה is the Torah that protects.

steps.title: Arrested for one charge versus five
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: when רבי אלעזר בן פרטא and רבי חנינא בן תרדיון were arrested, רבי אלעזר said: you are fortunate to be held on one charge, and woe to me, held on five.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: When רבי אלעזר בן פרטא and רבי חנינא בן תרדיון were arrested, רבי אלעזר בן פרטא said to רבי חנינא בן תרדיון: You are fortunate, since you were arrested for one thing. Woe is me, since I was arrested for five things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main topic, the Romans arresting חכמים, and starts a new ברייתא. This opening line sets up the story that will continue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר thinks he is in more danger, because he faces five charges and his friend faces only one. In the next step, רבי חנינא answers him and turns this comparison around.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When Rabbi Elazar ben Perata was arrested
together with Rabbi Ḥanina ben Teradyon,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Perata said
to Rabbi Ḥanina ben Teradyon:
Fortunate are you, for you were arrested on one charge;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹי לִי שֶׁנִּתְפַּסְתִּי עַל חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים.
phrases.english: woe is me, for I was arrested on five charges.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן כְּשֶׁנִּתְפְּסוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about מזמה and goes back to the stories of arrested חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא saw himself in greater danger, with five charges against his friend's one.

steps.title: רבי חנינא flips the comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן תרדיון answers that רבי אלעזר is the lucky one. He was arrested on five charges but will be saved, because he did both Torah and גמילות חסדים. רבי חנינא only learned Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said to him: You are fortunate. You were arrested on five charges, and you will be saved. Woe is me. I was arrested on one charge, and I will not be saved. You were busy with Torah and with acts of kindness, but I was busy only with Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues, and רבי חנינא answers רבי אלעזר. He says the opposite of what רבי אלעזר said: רבי אלעזר will be saved and רבי חנינא will not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר judged by the number of charges against them. רבי חנינא judges by their merits: Torah together with גמילות חסדים protects a person, but Torah alone does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said to him:
Fortunate are you, for you were arrested on five charges
and you will be saved;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹי לִי שֶׁנִּתְפַּסְתִּי עַל דָּבָר אֶחָד
phrases.english: woe is me, for I was arrested on one charge
and I will not be saved,
because you were busy with Torah and with acts of kindness,
while I was busy only with Torah alone.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 8 with רבי חנינא's reply, which reverses רבי אלעזר's assessment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah together with גמילות חסדים saves a person. Torah alone does not.

steps.title: רב הונא: Torah alone is like having no God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי חנינא's words match רב הונא. רב הונא says that someone who only learns Torah, without acts of kindness, is like someone who has no God. He learns this from a פסוק in דברי הימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches רב הונא, who said: Anyone who is busy only with Torah is like someone who has no God. As it says: "Now for many days Israel was without the true God..." What does "without the true God" mean? It means that anyone who is busy only with Torah is like someone who has no God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רב הונא that supports what רבי חנינא just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא implied that Torah alone was not enough to save him. רב הונא gives this a source: the פסוק describes a time of being 'without the true God,' and he reads it as describing someone who learns but does no kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is in line with רב הונא
One who is busy with Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a lasting lesson: Torah learning has to be joined with acts of kindness.

phrases.english: And this is like Rav Huna,
for Rav Huna said:
Anyone who is busy only with Torah
is like someone who has no God,
as it says:
"Now for many days Israel was
without the true God, etc."
What does "without the true God" mean?
That anyone who is busy only with Torah
is like someone who has no God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי חנינא's statement with a teaching of רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's claim that Torah alone, without גמילות חסדים, would not save him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's reading of the פסוק 'וימים רבים לישראל ללא אלהי אמת'.

steps.title: But רבי חנינא ran the charity fund
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי חנינא did no גמילות חסדים. A ברייתא says people should only give charity if a scholar like רבי חנינא בן תרדיון is in charge of the fund.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he really not do acts of kindness? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: A person should not put his money into the charity purse unless a Torah scholar like רבי חנינא בן תרדיון is in charge of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי חנינא could say he lacked kindness. A ברייתא shows he was the model charity supervisor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי חנינא was held up as the ideal person to run the charity fund, it seems he was deeply involved in צדקה. That clashes with his claim that he only learned Torah.

phrases.english: And he was not busy with acts of kindness?
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
A person should not give his money
to the charity purse

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מְמוּנֶּה עָלָיו תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
phrases.english: unless a Torah scholar is in charge of it
like Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual claim in step 9 that רבי חנינא did only Torah.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's statement that he did not engage in גמילות חסדים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא names him as the ideal charity supervisor, which suggests he was involved in charity.

steps.title: Trusted, but did not give himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא was trusted to handle other people's charity money honestly, but he did not give charity himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was trusted to be reliable, but actually doing charity himself, he did not do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating managing charity from giving it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only proves that he was honest and reliable with the money. It does not prove that he gave his own money to the poor, so his claim of lacking גמילות חסדים still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: As for doing it, he did not do it

steps.confusionAlert: Being trusted with charity money is not the same as giving charity. The ברייתא praised his honesty, not his giving.

phrases.english: He was trusted to be reliable,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the corrected wording has the word in square brackets. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: but actually doing it himself, he did not do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: being a trusted supervisor versus personally giving charity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Supervising the charity fund means he did גמילות חסדים.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only trusted to manage the fund and did not give himself.

steps.title: But he gave his Purim money to the poor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Another ברייתא says רבי חנינא's own Purim money got mixed up with charity money, and he gave all of it to the poor. That shows he did give himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that he said to him: My Purim money got mixed up with charity money, and I gave it all out to the poor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to show רבי חנינא did give charity from his own pocket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer said he never gave himself. This story shows him giving his own Purim money to the poor, so that answer seems wrong.

phrases.english: But it was taught: he said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי חנינא speaking, in a story about him and רבי יוסי בן קיסמא.

phrases.english: My Purim money got mixed up
with charity money,
and I gave them out to the poor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12 that he did not give charity himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that מיעבד לא עבד, meaning he did not personally give.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He gave his own Purim money to the poor, so he did personally give charity.

steps.title: He gave, but not as much as he should have
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי חנינא did give charity, but not as much as was fitting for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did give, but he did not give as much as he should have.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final answer that fits all the sources together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is changed from 'he did not give at all' to 'he did not give enough.' This fits the Purim story and still explains why רבי חנינא felt he lacked גמילות חסדים.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as was fitting for him, as he should have

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא did do charity, just not enough for his level. Even great Torah scholars are judged on their kindness, as רב הונא taught.

phrases.english: He did give,
but he did not give as much as he should have.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶיעְבַּד עֲבַד, כִּדְבָעֵי לֵיהּ לָא עֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by refining the answer of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refinement: from not giving at all to not giving enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: He gave, but less than was fitting for him.

steps.title: The Romans charge רבי אלעזר בן פרטא with two crimes
steps.stepSummary: The Romans bring רבי אלעזר בן פרטא to trial and ask why he taught Torah and why he stole.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought רבי אלעזר בן פרטא to trial. They said: Why did you teach Torah, and why did you steal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of the sages on trial. The Romans now question רבי אלעזר בן פרטא about two charges. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching Torah was against Roman law at the time, so it was a crime in their eyes. He is also accused of robbery. The two charges together are what his clever answer will take apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who was arrested along with רבי חנינא בן תרדיון

phrases.english: They brought Rabbi Elazar ben Perata,
they said: Why did you teach Torah,
and why did you steal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְיוּהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא, אֲמַרוּ: מַאי טַעְמָא תָּנֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רבי חנינא's charity and returns to the trial story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he committed the two crimes he is accused of: teaching Torah and stealing.

steps.title: A robber can't be a scholar, so both charges fall
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא answers that a robber and a scholar can't be the same person. Since one charge is false, the other is false too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If someone is a sword-carrying robber, he is not a man of books. If he is a man of books, he is not a robber. Since one of these is not true, the other is not true either.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא answers both charges with one argument. He says the two charges cancel each other out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that nobody is both a violent robber and a Torah scholar. So the charges contradict each other. He then denies both of them, since one is clearly false and the other falls along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with a sword, an armed robber
A man of books, a scholar
It is not so, it doesn't exist

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי סַיָּיפָא לָא סָפְרָא,
phrases.english: He said to them: If one is an armed robber, he is not a scholar,
and if one is a scholar, he is not an armed robber,
and since this one is not true, that one is also not true.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי סַיָּיפָא לָא סָפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two charges from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The charges contradict each other, so both are false.

steps.title: Then why do people call you רבי
steps.stepSummary: The Romans push back: if he doesn't teach Torah, why is he called ‘רבי’?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they call you ‘רבי’?
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans try to catch him. His title ‘רבי’ seems to show he is a Torah teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He had denied being a scholar. The Romans point to his title as evidence that he does teach Torah, which would bring back the first charge.

phrases.english: And why do they call you ‘Rabbi’?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges his denial in step 16 that he is a scholar.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he has the title ‘רבי’ if he is not a Torah teacher.

steps.title: He is the master of weavers
steps.stepSummary: He answers that he is called ‘רבי’ because he is a master weaver.
steps.simpleTranslation: I am the master of the weavers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא explains his title in a way that has nothing to do with Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רבן just means ‘master’ or ‘teacher’. He claims he is a master of a craft, weaving, so the title does not prove he teaches Torah.

phrases.english: I am the master of weavers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about his title.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ‘רבי’ refers to being a master weaver, not a Torah teacher.

steps.title: The Romans test him with two coils of wool
steps.stepSummary: To check his claim, the Romans bring two coils and ask which is the warp and which is the woof.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him two coils of thread. They said to him: Which one is the warp and which one is the woof?
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans test whether he really is a master weaver. This sets up the miracle in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real expert weaver would know the difference between the two kinds of thread right away. If he can't tell, his excuse falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Warp, the threads that run lengthwise on the loom
Woof, the threads woven crosswise through the warp

phrases.english: They brought him two coils of thread,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הֵי דְּשִׁתְיָא וְהֵי דְּעִרְבָּא?
phrases.english: they said to him: Which is the warp and which is the woof?
phrases.notes: These are the two sets of threads in weaving: one runs lengthwise, the other is woven across it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the claim he made in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether he can tell warp from woof, to prove he is a weaver.

steps.title: Hornets miraculously show him the answer
steps.stepSummary: A female hornet lands on the warp and a male hornet on the woof, and he answers correctly.
steps.simpleTranslation: A miracle happened for him. A female hornet came and sat on the warp, and a male hornet came and sat on the woof. He said to them: This one is the warp and that one is the woof.
steps.whatsHappening: A miracle helps him pass the test. He uses the hornets as a sign and names each coil correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The female hornet marked the warp and the male hornet marked the woof, and he understood the hint. Heaven itself is backing up his answer, so the Romans' test fails.

phrases.english: A miracle happened for him:
a female hornet came
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the corrected wording has the one in square brackets. Both mean 'came'.

phrases.english: and sat on the warp,
and a male hornet came and sat on the woof.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הַאי דְּשִׁתְיָא וְהַאי דְּעִרְבָּא.
phrases.english: He said to them: This is the warp and this is the woof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the weaving test from step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With the help of the hornets, he correctly names the warp and the woof.

steps.title: Why didn't you come to בי אבידן
steps.stepSummary: The Romans ask why he did not attend the gathering at בי אבידן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: And why didn't you come to the house of אבידן?
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans bring a new complaint against him. This sets up his excuse in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh charge, separate from the earlier ones. Staying away from this place seems to be held against him as a sign of disloyalty.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of אבידן, a gathering place

phrases.english: They said to him: And why
didn't you come to the house of Avidan?
phrases.notes: This was a meeting place where people held debates.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָתֵית לְבֵי אֲבִידָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new charge after the weaving test is over.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he stayed away from בי אבידן.

steps.title: He was old and afraid of being trampled
steps.stepSummary: He answers that he was old and afraid the crowds would trample him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I was old, and I was afraid you might trample me with your feet.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא gives a harmless reason for staying away. He says it was about his safety, not disloyalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He turns the charge into a matter of old age and crowds. If his fear was real, then staying away was not a crime.

phrases.english: He said to them: I was old
and I was afraid that perhaps you would trample me with your feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He stayed away because he was old and feared the crowds.

steps.title: How many old men were ever trampled
steps.stepSummary: The Romans mock his excuse. Up until now, how many old men have actually been trampled there?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: And until now, how many old men have been trampled?
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans attack his excuse. They say his fear is made up because no old man has ever been trampled there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on whether his fear is realistic. If nobody was ever hurt there, his excuse looks like a cover story.

phrases.english: [They said:] And until now
phrases.notes: The corrected wording adds 'they said', but either way it's still the Romans talking.

phrases.english: how many old men have been trampled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the excuse given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: His claim that he feared being trampled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No old man has ever been trampled there, so the fear is not believable.

steps.title: That very day an old man was trampled
steps.stepSummary: A miracle happened, and on that day one old man was trampled, which proved his fear was real.
steps.simpleTranslation: A miracle happened: on that very day one old man was trampled.
steps.whatsHappening: The story answers the Romans' challenge with a miracle. What he said he was afraid of actually happens that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Romans claimed his fear was groundless. Heaven arranged that an old man was trampled that day, so his excuse now looks completely reasonable. The ‘miracle’ is the timing, which saves him.

phrases.english: A miracle happened:
on that day one old man was trampled.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is happy that a man got hurt. The ‘miracle’ is that the timing proved רבי אלעזר בן פרטא's excuse true and saved his life.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְרְחִישׁ נִיסָּא, הַהוּא יוֹמָא אִירְמַס חַד סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mocking challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His fear of being trampled seemed made up.
steps.terutzMaskana: An old man was trampled that very day, so his fear was shown to be real.

steps.title: Why did you free your slave
steps.stepSummary: The Romans bring another charge: why did he set his slave free?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did you set your slave free?
steps.whatsHappening: The Romans bring their last charge. This sets up his denial in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new accusation, separate from the earlier ones. He is accused of setting his slave free.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי טַעְמָא קָא שָׁבְקַתְּ עַבְדָּךְ לְחֵירוּת?
phrases.english: And why did you set your slave free?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא קָא שָׁבְקַתְּ עַבְדָּךְ לְחֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new charge after the בי אבידן question is settled.

steps.title: He denies it ever happened
steps.stepSummary: He says the story never happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: These things never happened.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא flatly denies this charge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time he doesn't give a clever reason. He simply says the event never took place. That sets up the threat of a witness in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֹא הָיוּ דְבָרִים מֵעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: He said to them: These things never happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֹא הָיוּ דְבָרִים מֵעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A full denial: it never happened.

steps.title: Someone stands up to testify against him
steps.stepSummary: One of the people there gets up to testify that he did free his slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of them got up to testify against him.
steps.whatsHappening: His denial is about to be challenged by a witness. This sets up אליהו stepping in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now he got past each charge. Here a real witness threatens to prove his denial false.

phrases.english: One [of them] stood up to testify against him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Threatens to disprove his denial from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: His denial that he freed his slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A witness is ready to testify that it did happen.

steps.title: אליהו scares off the witness
steps.stepSummary: אליהו, disguised as a Roman official, warns the witness that a miracle will save רבי אלעזר בן פרטא again, and testifying will only show the witness's own wickedness.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו came, looking like one of the important men of the government. He said to him: Since miracles happened for him in all the other cases, a miracle will happen for him in this one too, and you will only be showing how wicked you are.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו steps in to stop the witness. He points out that every other charge failed through a miracle, so this one will fail too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו's argument works from the pattern: a miracle saved him each time, so it will happen again. The witness gains nothing and only shows himself to be wicked. The next step shows the witness ignoring this warning, so the threat is not over yet.
steps.whatToRemember: In every charge against רבי אלעזר בן פרטא, a miracle or a heavenly messenger came to save him. That is the big contrast with the harsh punishment of רבי חנינא בן תרדיון in the same trial.

phrases.english: Eliyahu came and appeared to him
as one of the important men of the government,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִדְּאִתְרְחִישׁ לֵיהּ נִיסָּא בְּכוּלְּהוּ,
phrases.english: he said to him: Since a miracle happened for him in all of them,
in this one too a miracle will happen for him,
and that man is only showing his own wickedness.
phrases.notes: 'That man' is a polite way of saying 'you'. Some versions have the round-bracket word, the corrected wording has the square-bracket one; both mean 'shows'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא אֵלִיָּהוּ אִידְּמִי לֵיהּ כְּחַד מֵחַשִּׁובֵי דְּמַלְכוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stops the witness threat from step 27.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witness's testimony would prove him guilty.
steps.terutzMaskana: Given the pattern of miracles, testifying would fail and only show the witness's wickedness. The witness ignores this, and the actual rescue comes in step 30.

steps.title: The witness ignores the warning and stands to testify
steps.stepSummary: Despite אליהו's warning, the man gets up to give his testimony against רבי אלעזר בן פרטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he paid no attention to him, and he stood up to tell them.
steps.whatsHappening: The danger to רבי אלעזר בן פרטא comes back: the witness ignores אליהו and gets ready to testify. This sets up the next move, where we will see how the threat is stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אליהו's warning in step 28 did not work on its own. The threat from step 27 is now active again, so a real rescue is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He paid no attention to him

phrases.english: But he paid no attention to him,
phrases.notes: "Him" means אליהו, who had just warned the man not to testify.

phrases.english: and he stood up to say it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אַשְׁגַּח בֵּיהּ, קָם לְמֵימַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The witness rejects the warning given in step 28, so the threat continues.
steps.kashyaTarget: The safety of רבי אלעזר בן פרטא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A living witness to the freeing of the slave would sink his defense.

steps.title: אליהו throws the witness four hundred פרסאות away
steps.stepSummary: The witness is sent off carrying an important letter to the emperor, and אליהו throws him so far away that he never comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a letter written by important people of the empire, to be sent to the emperor's court, and they sent it with that man. אליהו came and threw him four hundred פרסאות. He went and never came back.
steps.whatsHappening: The miracle that אליהו promised now happens. The witness is carried far away, so he can never testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the only witness gone, the charge of freeing the slave collapses. This ends the trial of רבי אלעזר בן פרטא, who is saved by a miracle just as אליהו predicted in step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: פרסאות, a long unit of distance

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר בן פרטא is saved from every charge by miracles. This closes his story.

phrases.english: There was a written letter,
which was written by important people of the empire
to send to the emperor's court,
and they sent it with that man.
phrases.notes: "That man" is the witness who wanted to testify.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא אֵלִיָּהוּ פַּתְקֵיהּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה פַּרְסֵי,
phrases.english: Eliyahu came and threw him four hundred parasangs,
he went and did not come back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא אֵלִיָּהוּ פַּתְקֵיהּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה פַּרְסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This resolves the threat from step 29 through the miracle promised in step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witness would testify, and רבי אלעזר בן פרטא would be convicted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The witness is carried away and never returns, so there is no testimony.

steps.title: The Romans ask רבי חנינא בן תרדיון why he learned תורה
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: רבי חנינא בן תרדיון is brought to trial for learning תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought רבי חנינא בן תרדיון. They said to him: Why were you busy with תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from רבי אלעזר בן פרטא to the second prisoner, רבי חנינא בן תרדיון, and the Romans question him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The charge here is simply learning תורה, which the Romans had banned. Unlike רבי אלעזר בן פרטא, he will not deny it, and that sets up a very different ending.

phrases.english: They brought Rabbi Ḥanina ben Teradyon,
they said to him:
Why were you occupied with Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This starts the trial of the second prisoner after the first one ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he broke the Roman ban on learning תורה

steps.title: He answers that ה׳ commanded him
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן תרדיון openly admits it and quotes a פסוק saying he learns because ה׳ commanded him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: "As ה׳ my God commanded me."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בן תרדיון answers with a פסוק. He does not deny anything. He says plainly that he learns תורה because ה׳ commanded it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where רבי אלעזר בן פרטא denied the charges, רבי חנינא בן תרדיון admits his learning and explains it as a command from ה׳. This open admission leads straight to his sentence.

phrases.english: He said to them:
"As the Lord my God commanded me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוַּנִי ה׳ אֱלֹהָי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the Romans' question in step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns תורה because ה׳ commanded him to.

steps.title: The harsh sentences on him, his wife and his daughter
steps.stepSummary: The Romans immediately sentence him to burning, his wife to execution, and his daughter to be placed in a brothel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away they sentenced him to burning, his wife to execution, and his daughter to sit in a brothel.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reports the Romans' immediate sentences against רבי חנינא בן תרדיון and his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each family member gets a different punishment. This sets up the גמרא's next discussion, which explains why each one received that particular sentence.

phrases.english: Immediately they sentenced him to burning,
and his wife to execution,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל בִּתּוֹ לֵישֵׁב בְּקוּבָּה שֶׁל זוֹנוֹת.
phrases.english: and his daughter to sit in a brothel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The sentences follow directly from his open admission in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning for him, execution for his wife, and a brothel for his daughter.

steps.title: Starting to explain why he was sentenced to burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why רבי חנינא בן תרדיון deserved the punishment of burning from Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Him to burning, because he used to...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts explaining the reason for his burning, and the sentence finishes on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that a sentence like this also reflects a decree from Heaven. It begins looking for something he did that would explain the punishment, starting with his own sentence.
steps.confusionAlert: The Romans are not the ones giving this reason. The גמרא itself is explaining why Heaven allowed this punishment to happen.

phrases.english: Him to burning, because he used to

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins explaining the first sentence listed in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His burning had a reason from Heaven, which the גמרא is about to give.
